bluf: On The Map Marketing is a Miami local search agency, with an office in Riga, Latvia, selling SEO, PPC, digital PR and web builds to law firms, home services and healthcare practices. The record shows a case library dated almost entirely to July 2025, mostly injury firm results, and weekly law firm blog posts to 2026-07-21, but no dated moves, news or open roles, so where it is going is not on file. Its book holds 16 clients, 10 observed and 6 names only. A rival should know that it sells paid search and runs 0 Google ads of its own, and that it has no AI search line.
doing:
On The Map Marketing sells local search to small practices. Its positioning line, a "local search marketing powerhouse" offering SEO, marketing and web design specialised by industry for law firms, home services and healthcare practices, means: put a practice into map and local results and build the site it ranks with. The headline claim is scale plus two multiples, "1,000+ companies" served, Wagner Reese at 14.53x ROI and Hipskind & McAninch at 18.6x case revenue from SEO; the page title styles it the #1 US digital marketing agency. Headcount reads 50+ on the about page, 40+ on the careers page.

The sold mix leads with SEO and Local, both scored 3: Local SEO and Multi Location SEO sit in the navigation, and SEO cases for two injury firms back the score. Content & Digital PR, Paid Search and Web & Product score 2, on a Wagner Reese case of 41 media features and 25 backlinks plus a reactive PR case, PPC cases for Nunez Law, Angelika Film Center, another law firm and a NY dental office, and a portfolio of 30+ site builds with development run from Riga. AI Search / GEO, AI Automation, Data & Measurement, Email & CRM, CRO and Paid Social score 0. The record lists no proprietary product and no partner.

Its AI posture is silence: no posture statement, no AI line, no llms.txt, 1 AI topic URL in the sitemap. The record lists no dated moves, news, open roles or pricing signal; the dated activity is 14 case studies running from a dental PPC case dated 2023-10-06 to the Wagner Reese thought leadership PR case dated 2025-07-29. Conspicuously absent for an agency selling local work to injury and home service firms: any LSA or Sponsored Places work, which the Horus P3 note flags, and any healthcare case newer than that dental one, though healthcare sits in its positioning line.
clients:
The client type is local: law (personal injury, criminal defense, family, immigration, workers' compensation), trades (plumbing, roofing, HVAC, contracting) and practices (plastic surgery, chiropractic, med spa, dental), sold from Miami. The needs read holds 16 clients, 10 observed and 6 names only; local and lead generation (5 clients) and organic demand (4) lead the mix.

Wagner Reese came for PR and local leads ("How Wagner Reese Built Authority With Thought Leadership PR", 2025-07-29, and a 1353% ROI case for targeted SEO). Hipskind & McAninch, a Belleville trial firm, came for organic demand (+1763% case revenue, 2025-07-17); Roberts Law Firm, an Orange County car accident practice, for organic leads (up 150% in 18 months). Nunez Law came for paid performance, leads and web build (5.61% conversion in 2 months), Hansford McDaniel for paid performance (4.66x ROI with PPC), 844 See Mike for reactive PR (738 media features), GTW Lawyers for social (92.5% more engagement). Beyond law, Angelika Film Center, an arthouse cinema chain, came for paid performance and brand (1960% ROI in tickets), GWS Pressure Cleaning and Miami Top Cleaning for organic demand.

Angel Reyes is coded names only although its slug title claims 1317 media placements; R + R Dental and Weber Law appear in case studies but not in the needs read. The Desiah Law Firm, Ferguson Hill Filous Attorneys At Law, Caputo & Van Der Walde, LLP, Meyers Injury Law and US Patriot Steel sit on portfolio pages with no described work, so a web build need is inferred. No client is shared with another tracked agency.

Under KJ4 (the platforms absorbing the execution layer) it is likely, moderate confidence, that the PPC clients will need LSA and Sponsored Places work the record does not show; under KJ8 the injury firms buying attorney PR likely keep that need.
house: Say and do: two lines tested, one practised. Paid search is contradicted: it sells PPC and the Transparency Center shows 0 Google ads of its own, 0 in the last 30 days, although its site carries a Google Ads tag; with no ads there is no sample line to quote. Publishing cadence is corroborated: the sitemap lists 556 URLs, 5 updated in 90 days and 120 in 365, and the newest blog posts on record run a week apart from 2026-06-16 to 2026-07-21, all law firm topics, one on email marketing, a line it scores 0. The LinkedIn check finds 0 ads ("0 ads match the name query"). The tag stack on WordPress is GTM, GA4, Google Ads, Meta Pixel, HubSpot and Microsoft Clarity, with no test tools and no ABM stack. It publishes no llms.txt and blocks no AI crawlers. The Radar flags one gap: the missing Google ads.
market:
The Horus read puts it at a tailwind index of -12.3, band Exposed, percentile 6. It is best placed for KJ8 (human provenance becomes a distribution signal), driven by Creator & Influencer and Content & Digital PR, with a smaller KJ2 tailwind from Paid Search, and most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle hollowed out), driven by SEO, Paid Search and Content & Digital PR, and KJ4 (platforms absorbing the execution layer), driven by Paid Search. Best scenario fit: The Walled Oasis at 46/100. It is partial on P3 (LSAs and Sponsored Places) and P4 (inputs automation runs on), absent on P1, P2, P6, P7 and P8, unknown on P5.

The Monsoon read is 79.7, band Landfall, percentile 99: migration 73.7 against displacement 85.7. The sold mix supplies 74 of the index, SEO (21) and Local (20) carrying the most movable hours; the work would go 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America. The footprint is inferred: no hub office listed, though the record places development in Riga, and no onshore claim.
openings:
The strongest opening is the paid search contradiction: it sells PPC to injury firms, carries a Google Ads tag on its own site, and the Transparency Center shows 0 ads of its own. The record also shows no LSA or Sponsored Places work (P3 partial) and no test of ads inside AI assistants (P8 absent). It is likely, moderate confidence, that its PPC clients, Nunez Law, Hansford McDaniel and Angelika Film Center, are contestable by a rival that shows its own live ads and runs LSAs as core local work. Falsifier: a later compile listing its own ads in the Transparency Center.

Healthcare is the softest vertical: named in the positioning line, evidenced by one dental PPC case dated 2023-10-06, so a rival with current practice proof likely wins there (low confidence). With 6 of its 16 clients names only, and no feed, schema or entity work on its core SEO and web lines (P2 absent), the proof is thin at the edges. Displacement at 85.7 says the book buys on price: an offshore delivered rival can likely undercut it line by line, and an outcome priced offer (P5 unknown) is a conversation it cannot have in public.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, due October 2026: output or outcome pricing at a top five holdco would sharpen KJ6, its main headwind, against an agency whose record lists no pricing model.

I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, next reading 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas or engagement would strengthen KJ8, the tailwind its PR line rides.
I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt out rates, December 2026 to January 2027: high opt out rates would slow KJ4, the judgment behind its Paid Search exposure.
The Transparency Center count of 0 Google ads: ads under its name in a later compile would close the paid search contradiction and retire the strongest opening.
The case library, newest dated 2025-07-29, and the blog, newest post 2026-07-21: a new healthcare, LSA or AI search case would change the openings on those lines.
